references.text: The parallel version of the Sabbath commandment in Exodus, which also forbids work on the seventh day for the entire household, including servants, animals, and foreigners.
Repeats the Sabbath commandment with emphasis on rest for oxen, donkeys, and servants, as well as the foreigner.
Emphasizes the holiness of the Sabbath and the prohibition against work on the seventh day.
Moses delivers the Sabbath commandment to the congregation of Israel, forbidding work on the seventh day.
Describes the Sabbath as a holy assembly where no work is to be done.
Ezekiel refers to the Sabbath commandment that God gave Israel as a sign between Himself and them.
Nehemiah rebukes the people for breaking the Sabbath by working and trading on the holy day.
Jesus discusses the meaning of the Sabbath and declares that the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.
Jesus says that the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
The synagogue ruler refers to the six days of work in contrast to the Sabbath, and Jesus responds about untying animals on the Sabbath.
